stories.headline: Lombard's incredible slide, tiebreaking homer lift Yanks over Rays. Schlitter finishes with 1.95 ERA
stories.summary: — Rookie George Lombard Jr. scored on an incredible slide and followed with a tiebreaking. two-run homer as Cam Schlitter finished his season with an AL-best 1.95 ERA in the New York Yankees' 6-4 comeback win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday night.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- — Rookie George Lombard Jr. scored on an incredible slide and followed with a tiebreaking. two-run homer as Cam Schlitter finished his season with an AL-best 1.95 ERA in the New York Yankees' 6-4 comeback win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday night.


Lombard, who debuted on Aug. 4, had three RBI for the Yankees (92-67), who overcame a 4-0 deficit. He hit an RBI double in the seventh, jumped over catcher Liam Hicks to score in the eighth and followed with his fourth homer in seven games.


Austin Wells started New York’s comeback with a sixth-inning homer off Jake Woodford and Lombard cut the deficit to 4-2 in the three-run seventh.


He took third on Brady Hopkins' wild pitch and scored when another pitch bounced to the backstop. As the ball caromed back to Hicks, Lombard popped up well in front of the plate on his feet-first slide and jumped over the catcher while twisting his body in fair territory and reaching down to slap his right hand on the plate.


Paul Goldschmidt followed with a single that tied the score 4-4.


Lombard hit his seventh home run of the season in the eighth, driving a sinker from Steven Matz (5-6) into the left field second deck. Lombard briefly watched the ball soar into the seats before starting his home run trot.


Making his final start before the AL Wild Card Series next week, Schlitter allowed two runs — one earned — in three innings. The 25-year-old right-hander went 14-6 and struck out 239 over 193 2/3 innings in his first full major league season. He finished with the Yankees' third-lowest ERA for a qualified pitcher behind Spud Chandler’s 1.64 ERA in 1943 and Ron Guidry’s 1.74 ERA in 1978, according to the team.


Tampa Bay (96-63), which clinched the AL East on Tuesday, built a 4-0 lead as Junior Caminero drove in two runs to raise his RBI total to 99. The Rays got a pair of unearned runs, helped by errors from right fielder Heliot Ramos and reliever Luis Gil.


Bradley Hanner (1-0) retired Caminero with a runner on to end the eighth and stranded a runner in the ninth for his first major league win.


Up next
Rays: RHP Freddy Peralta (9-11, 4.56, ERA) faces LHP Cristopher Sánchez (18-6, 2.92) in the opener of a three-game series in Philadelphia Friday night.


Yankees: Host Baltimore in a single-admission doubleheader on Friday.


------

stories.headline: Anthony Gordon: Premier League players most fatigued at summer tournaments
stories.summary: Anthony Gordon has said Premier League players are destined to come into summer tournaments more fatigued than any other league.
stories.body:
Anthony Gordon has said Premier League players are destined to come into summer tournaments more fatigued than any other league.

The inquest into England's painful World Cup semifinal defeat to Argentina continues, with focus on their energy-sapping style of football and inability to keep the ball in the same way that Spain can.

Boss Tuchel said fatigue played a part in their capitulation, coming on the back of extra time in their quarterfinal win against Norway in Miami heat and emotionally-draining victories against Congo DR and Mexico.

Gordon says those playing in the relentlessness of the Premier League are at a disadvantage at the back end of tournaments.

"I think that would probably be a fact," he said. "I don't know the stats, but I think for sure because in England, I'm not saying there is an easy game in any other leagues, but every game is as hard as the next.

"Playing Arsenal is the same as playing a newly-promoted side. That's the difficulty of the Premier League. Every game is so intense. Anyone can win a game.

"I mean, I think Hull, a newly-promoted team, were unbeaten until they played Newcastle.

"So that shows the strength of the Premier League, the strength of the English game, and I think for the English players playing in the Premier League, it would be a lot tougher on the body than players elsewhere."

Gordon's substitution in the semifinal remains a big talking point -- he was withdrawn 16 minutes after putting his side 1-0 up and replaced by a defender.

- Tuchel's England dilemma: Emulate Spain or embrace Premier League 'chaos'?

- Bukayo Saka: 'Tough' to stay on England bench in Argentina World Cup loss

- Harry Kane: Argentina defeat was most painful England moment yet

The game quickly unravelled after that and Gordon said that match needed a lot of unpacking in his personal diary afterwards.

"It was more than one page, I can tell you that," he added. "Maybe not consistently, but I always like to write things down. It just makes you feel more clear.

"I think everyone does that in a different way. Some people use laptops, or some people don't like to do anything.

"My version of that has always been just to write it down, and I kind of like it because I can look back on it and pass it on to my kids.

"But the Argentina game was probably the most memorable one I've had because I didn't really know what to write. I wrote down just pure emotion of what I felt.

"Obviously, I won't go into those details, but it was it was a good few pages, I can tell you."

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Tsarukyan; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Volkanovski.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Cris Cyborg; 5. Alexa Grasso; 6. Manon Fiorot; 7. Dakota Ditcheva; 8. Natalia Silva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Zhang; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Blanchfield; 8. Ditcheva; 9. Suarez; 10. Fiorot.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Fiorot; 10. Suarez.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: Rolling Stone shows who is Dolphin boss
stories.summary: Dolphins' warrior Ray Stone will retire at the season's end as the side's unsmiling assassin who gets the job done no matter what pain he has to play through.
stories.body:
Ray Stone has claims to being the toughest man in the NRL.

Not that the Dolphins' warrior would care two hoots for the title as he nears retirement at the end of the 2026 season at the tender age of 29.

But there was a reason coach Kristian Woolf singled him out at last year's presentation night for playing the last six rounds with a broken hand and final 15 rounds with needles in both shoulders.

He had off-season shoulder surgery after pushing himself to play when the Dolphins had multiple forwards on the injured list.

Stone is one of those players who performs when busted. When fit and relatively injury-free, though, he is even more dangerous.

"There are a lot of tough men who play our game but he is in the top group," Woolf told AAP.

"It is not just his toughness, it's his commitment to the team that I really admire.

"He is just a guy who refuses to let his teammates down. It doesn't matter if it is playing injured, he is making an effort on a kick-chase, getting into a tackle or a carry.

"I love his hit-ups off the kick-off. I get a kick out of watching those because he runs so hard. He is just committed to the team. That is what we are going to miss."

Stone has been linked to a boxing career but AAP understands he has obtained multiple tickets in trade areas and will only get in a ring if he sees fit. He can hold them up, as the saying goes.

"It is probably based on family time for me," Stone said, when asked why he was calling time.

"The kids are getting a bit older and I am quite busy on weekends so I want to be a part of that."

Woolf wanted him on deck on 2027.

"I have spoken to him a number of times and asked if I could change his mind but he has got other things in life he wants to do," the coach said.

"I respect that about him. He knows what he wants. He has pushed himself through the pain."

Stone was the second player signed at the Dolphins after starting his NRL career at Parramatta, where he played 31 matches in five seasons. At the Dolphins, he has notched 81 games in four years..

"The reason I came up here was for opportunity," he said.

"I was in and out of first-grade at Parramatta where we had a strong team and I spoke to Wayne Bennett about coming here and he said I'd be more of a consistent first-grader."

The warhorse, who plays mostly off the bench, has scored eight tries for the Dolphins but, like an old-school footy player of the past, he doesn't smile after any.

"It's not something I stress about," Stone said, through gritted teeth.

"I like to leave all my celebrating until after the game when the boys have got the result."

He's done plenty of that this year, with the Dolphins winning 16 of their last 18 matches ahead of the preliminary final against Sydney Roosters.

"This year I've been a lot healthier and the squad has too, which has definitely helped our middle rotation," Stone said.

"Last year, pretty much our whole starting pack was in rehab. The minutes have been distributed a lot more which has helped me stay healthy."

Woolf is just glad to have Stone in the team after he missed the early rounds with his shoulder recovery.

"We did miss him too. He is a small man in a big man's world who plays so tough," Woolf said.

"He is loved, respected and will be missed next year.

"He is going to leave a legacy that people don't realise. There are no discipline issues around Ray. He turns up and gets his job done every day of every week."

stories.headline: Falcons upset Packers in Michael Penix Jr.'s return from ACL
stories.summary: Bijan Robinson and Drake London couldn't be stopped, as Atlanta ended Green Bay's streak of 13 straight home-opening wins.
stories.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Have the real Atlanta Falcons stood up?

After one of the most futile offensive stretches in NFL history over the first two weeks of the season, the Falcons looked reborn in a 35-14 win over the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night at Lambeau Field. Michael Penix Jr.'s return from a torn ACL reignited the team's offense in an impressive performance on the road in primetime against a depleted Packers team playing without edge rusher Micah Parsons (ACL) and running back Josh Jacobs (commissioner exempt list).

Penix was 18-of-25 passing for 256 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He settled down after throwing a pick on his third pass.

Penix's presence opened up the running game, which was dominant to the tune of 244 yards on the ground. Bijan Robinson had 194 of those with a touchdown and Brian Robinson Jr. added a touchdown, as well. Falcons wide receiver Drake London had nine catches for 194 yards.

The Falcons' defense stymied Packers quarterback Jordan Love all game, taking advantage of a Green Bay offensive line that was missing two starters and Jacobs.

Love was 28-of-52 for 312 yards, two touchdowns and one interceptions. The Packers had only 17 rushing yards.

Over the first two weeks of the season, the Falcons, led by third-string quarterback Cooper Rush, scored 16 combined points, a league low. Atlanta had 17 points by halftime Thursday night. And the Falcons were able to end a 27-drive streak without a red zone snap, which is tied for the second longest to start a season over the last 45 years.

Atlanta Falcons (1-2)

QB performance: It started off disastrously for Michael Penix Jr., who threw an interception on his first series of the game. But the third-year quarterback settled in nicely in his season debut once the second quarter hit. Penix was 13-of-15 passing in the second and third quarters -- with a touchdown to tight end Austin Hooper -- and a perfect 5-of-5 on third downs over that stretch.

Stat to know: In the first quarter, the Falcons ended their streak of 27 consecutive drives to start the season without taking a snap in the red zone. That is tied with the 1997 Detroit Lions for the second longest streak in the past 45 seasons, per ESPN Research. The 1992 Patriots had the longest at 34.

Trend to watch: The Falcons put star cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. (groin) on injured reserve earlier this week, but the team's secondary got a boon from the return of corner Billy Bowman Jr., who tore his Achilles last November. Bowman, C.J. Henderson and Avieon Terrell, AJ's younger brother, did a great job keeping quarterback Jordan Love in check despite the loss of Terrell, whom Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich calls one of the league's top boundary corners. -- Marc Raimondi

Next game: Oct. 5 at New Orleans Saints

Green Bay Packers (1-2)

The Packers have more problems than just their offensive line, but if they don't give Jordan Love at least a couple more seconds to throw and also try to create at least some running lanes, then Love might not make it through the season healthy and the Packers might finish last in the league in rushing.

Right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (knee) is done for the season and left guard Aaron Banks (toe/knee) can't ever seem to stay healthy. They've started three different left guards in as many games, and the experiment with Jacob Monk at right guard hasn't worked, either.

Two weeks after Love was hit 15 times by the Vikings in the opener, the Falcons hit him 11 times.

Only once in Love's career as a starter have the Packers come back to win when trailing by double digits at halftime, and that was in his first home start in 2023 (down 17-0 against the Saints, they came back to win 18-17). Not only was there no comeback on Thursday, there wasn't even the threat of one.

The Packers have salvaged seasons before after 1-2 starts and edge rusher Micah Parsons will be back in a few weeks, but even that might not matter. They were booed off the field at halftime and the boos continued in the second half.

Most surprising performance: The Packers were off to a solid start defending the run -- until Thursday. Through two games, they allowed 87 rushing yards per game (eighth in the league) and held their opponents to 2.9 yards per carry (second best). And then they let Falcons running back Bijan Robinson run wild. He rushed for 111 yards in the first half alone. The Falcons totaled 244 rushing yards and averaged 6.3 yards per run. Robinson certainly did his part to create problems, but the Packers created some of their own problems with myriad missed tackles.

Stat to know: When Love heaved it to no one on fourth-and-1 from the Falcons' 7-yard line to start the second half, it was the Packers' fourth failed fourth-down conversion in as many attempts to start this season. That's the most attempts without a fourth-down conversion in the NFL this season.

Trend to watch: Maybe Josh Jacobs would have made somewhat of a difference, but without their leading rusher the past two seasons, the Packers have no running game. None. They came into the game dead last in the league in rushing yards per game (64.5) and now that number will get even lower after they rushed for only 17 yards. Of course, they ran only nine times because they were behind most of the game, but when they did run, they got nowhere. MarShawn Lloyd carried four times for 11 yards. Kaleb Johnson carried four times for six yards. -- Rob Demovsky

Next game: Oct. 4 at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

stories.headline: WNBA playoffs 2026: Mystics lock in 5-seed, Fever are No. 6
stories.summary: Minnesota, Las Vegas, Golden State, Indiana, Atlanta, New York, Washington and Dallas are headed to the playoffs.
stories.body:
The bracket is nearly set. The Washington Mystics are the No. 5 seed by virtue of their win Thursday combined with a loss by the Indiana Fever, who will be the No. 6 seed.

All that's left: Will the defending champion Las Vegas Aces or Golden State Valkyries be the No. 2 seed?

All eight WNBA playoff spots were spoken for in August, but the final seeds weren't set until Thursday's regular-season finales.

Here's a look at the teams that will play in the postseason. Teams are listed in the order in which they clinched a playoff berth.

The WNBA playoffs open Sunday with four games.

Minnesota Lynx

Playoff seed: No. 1; will face New York in the first round

How they got here: The Lynx became the first team to clinch a spot in the postseason with a victory over the Wings on Aug. 9 that left Minnesota at 27-7 with 11 games to go in the regular season. Preseason expectations were tempered, as Napheesa Collier was still working her way back to the court after offseason surgery on both ankles and some key players were lost in free agency, but Minnesota has been at the top of the standings most of the summer. The Lynx won eight consecutive games over a three-week stretch in May and June and then 10 straight from July 8 through Aug. 2.

Point guard Olivia Miles (19.9 PPG, 6.1 APG), the No. 2 draft pick in April, adjusted immediately to the pro game and has been one of the top players in the league, putting in one of the most impressive rookie seasons in WNBA history. Guard Kayla McBride (18.2 PPG, 42.3% 3-point shooting) has also had highlight-reel moments, including a career-high 43 points and WNBA single-game record 10 3-pointers in that Aug. 9 win. Forward Natasha Howard anchored the frontcourt in Collier's absence and is averaging 15.1 points and 7.8 rebounds and shooting 58.7% from the field. And guard Courtney Williams (14.6 PPG, 5.1 RPG, 4.2 APG), who like Howard has started every game this season, remains ever-steady.

Key stat: Twenty-seven. Collier made her season debut on July 22. By then, the Lynx were 21-6 and had played 61% of their regular-season games and established Minnesota as the league leader without the perennial MVP candidate. The Lynx are 8-1 since Collier returned. She had 24 points and 10 boards in her first game back and is averaging 19.1 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.7 blocks and 1.2 steals. (Stats through games as of Aug. 16.)

Las Vegas Aces
Playoff seed: TBD

How they got here: The Aces became the second team to clinch a postseason berth, beating the Mystics on Aug. 13 to move to 24-11 with nine regular-season games remaining on their schedule. Last season, Las Vegas needed a second-half surge to turn around its season, ultimately winning the program's third WNBA championship. A'ja Wilson remains the engine -- averaging a league-best 26.1 points as well as 9.6 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 2.0 blocks and 1.5 steals, and shooting 52.3% -- but the Aces still have one of the league's best big three. Jackie Young (18.4 PPG, 6.7 APG) and Chelsea Gray (12.3 PPG, 7.1 APG) help anchor the backcourt along with Jewell Loyd (8.1 PPG), who continues to come off the bench this season. Forward NaLyssa Smith (12.0 PPG, 6.5 RPG) rounds out the double-digit scorers.

Key stat: Wilson has scored in double digits in every game this season (she has been held to 15 or fewer points in two games). Last season, she became the first player in WNBA history to win four regular-season MVP awards (she was also WNBA Finals MVP for the second time in her career). This season, she has made 33 3-pointers, setting a new single-season high (she had 31 in 2022). (Stats through games as of Aug. 16.)

Golden State Valkyries

Playoff seed: TBD

How they got here: A year ago, Golden State became the first WNBA expansion franchise to reach the playoffs in its first season. Now the Valkyries are going for a second straight year. With Monday's home win over Dallas, Golden State became the third team in 2026 to secure a postseason berth. Defense and depth lead the way, as the Valkyries -- who clinched with 10 regular-season games remaining and a 25-9 record -- give up the fewest points per game in the WNBA. Gabby Williams (14.6 PPG, 1.6 SPG), who joined Golden State as a free agent in the offseason, is one of the most impactful players on a new team this season. Fellow forward Janelle Salaun, the Sixth Player of the Year front-runner, ranks second on the team with 13.1 points per game despite coming off the bench. Guard Veronica Burton (12.3 PPG) rounds out the double-digit scorers.

Key stat: The Valkyries are 19-4 since June 9 after starting the season 6-5. Golden State has won six consecutive games -- the longest current win streak in the league. (Stats through games as of Aug. 17.)

Indiana Fever

Playoff seed: No. 6, opponent TBD

How they got here: The Fever lost to Dallas on Thursday, snapping their five-game winning streak. And even though they were idle Friday, they became the fourth team to clinch a playoff berth when Portland lost to Toronto. Guard Kelsey Mitchell (24.6 PPG) has been on a tear, scoring 20 or more points in a WNBA-record 21 consecutive games. On Thursday, she tallied her third career game with at least 35 points and five assists on 50% shooting from the field -- tied with A'ja Wilson, Diana Taurasi and Kelsey Plum for the most in WNBA history. Prior to the streak ending Thursday, Caitlin Clark (21.7 PPG, 8.3 APG) set a WNBA record with seven straight games with at least 20 points and at least five assists. Completing the big three, Aliyah Boston is averaging 16.9 points and 8.6 rebounds.

Key stat: The Fever have topped the 100-point mark in a WNBA-record 16 games this season -- five more than any other team in WNBA history. Indiana is headed to its third consecutive playoff appearance. Before the 2024 season, the Fever had missed the postseason for seven straight seasons. (Stats through games as of Aug. 21.)

Atlanta Dream

Playoff seed: No. 4, will face Washington in the first round

How they got here: Angel Reese scored a career-high 31 points and grabbed 14 rebounds -- her third consecutive game with at least 20 points and 10 boards -- on Saturday in a victory over Phoenix that clinched the Dream's playoff berth. This season, Reese has tallied 10 games with 20-plus points and 10-plus rebounds. (She had 10 combined in her first two seasons.) Reese also has 26 double-doubles on the season. Allisha Gray leads Atlanta in scoring (19.4 PPG), and Rhyne Howard (18.2 PPG) ranks second. The big three, who were voted All-Stars in July, help fuel the WNBA's third-highest scoring offense that has twice broken the franchise record this season for most points in a game (124 vs. the Sparks on Thursday). Guard Jordin Canada averages 7.4 assists, which ranks third in the WNBA.

Key Stat: Just two players in the WNBA are averaging a double-double: Reese (16.3 PPG, 12.0 RPG) and the Wings' Jessica Shepard (14.2 PPG, 11.1 RPG). (Stats through games as of Aug. 23.)

New York Liberty

Playoff seed: No. 8; will face Minnesota in the first round

How they got here: The Liberty clinched their playoff berth Sunday when the Fire lost. After a rocky start to coach Chris DeMarco's first year -- the team was 4-4 in late May and 13-11 in mid-July -- New York has won 10 of its last 13 games. Breanna Stewart (20.8 PPG, 8.1 RPG, 3.3 APG) remains one of the league's best players; her 46.8% shooting from the field is her best mark since 2022. Sabrina Ionescu, who missed 13 games because of injury, is averaging 15.9 points, 4.8 assists and 4.0 rebounds, and center Jonquel Jones, an All-Star alongside Stewart, adds 14.6 points and 9.2 rebounds per game. The return of Leonie Fiebich looks to be coming at the perfect time. The Liberty went 9-7 as she was out with a left foot injury, but she returned Saturday and had 20 points, five rebounds and five assists in a win over Indiana.

Key Stat: The Liberty have depth and talent throughout the roster. Not including Satou Sabally, who has played 15 games but none since June 23 because of lingering concussion symptoms, six players are averaging at least 9.0 points and 20 minutes per game, including Marine Johannes (9.0 PPG) and Pauline Astier (9.3 PPG, 3.4 APG). (Stats through games as of Aug. 24.)

Washington Mystics

Playoff seed: No. 5, will face Atlanta in the first round

How they got here: The Mystics clinched a berth Sunday; their win over the Fire combined with the Sky's loss the same night made Washington the seventh team to secure a playoff spot. In that 105-100 victory over Portland, Shakira Austin scored a career-high 31 points and had her first career game with 30 points and 10 rebounds. Austin (17.0 PPG, 9.6 RPG) leads Washington in scoring, though guard Sonia Citron (16.9 PPG) is right behind her. Kiki Iriafen (15.2 PPG, 9.3 RPG) has had three straight double-doubles.

Key Stat: The Mystics, the youngest team in the league, are back in the playoffs for the first time since 2023. (Stats through games as of Aug. 24.)

Dallas Wings

Playoff seed: No. 7, opponent TBD

How they got here: Paige Bueckers (20.6 PPG, 5.8 APG, 4.1 RPG), who scored 54 points over the past two games, has helped lead Dallas to its first playoff appearance since 2023. The Wings clinched the final berth Tuesday as all five starters scored in double figures in a win over Portland. Bueckers, who was the No. 1 draft pick in 2025 and will compete in her first playoffs, leads Dallas in scoring and assists. Jessica Shepard (14.2 PPG, 11.1 RPG), who has been one of the most impactful players on a new squad this season, is one of two players in the WNBA averaging a double-double. (Angel Reese is the other.) Arike Ogunbowale ranks second on the team with 15.1 PPG. Earlier this month, the Wings lost 2026 No. 1 pick Azzi Fudd (13.1 PPG) for the season to a knee injury. Young post player Awak Kuier (5.8 PPG, 3.5 RPG) could be heating up at the right time. She had one of her best games of the season -- 12 points, 12 rebounds and five blocks -- on Tuesday.

Key stat: The Wings improved to 23-16 on Tuesday. That's their most wins in any season since 2007, when the franchise was still in Detroit. Dallas has 20 90-point games this season, the most in a single campaign in franchise history. (Stats through games as of Aug. 25.)

stories.headline: Elly De La Cruz hits 30th homer and Reds rally for 7-6 win over Braves, who lock up NL's No. 3 seed
stories.summary: — Elly De La Cruz hit his 30th homer, Héctor Rodríguez and rookie Carlos Jorge also went deep, and the Cincinnati Reds rallied from an early deficit to beat the NL East champion Atlanta Braves 7-6 on Thursday night.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- — Elly De La Cruz hit his 30th homer, Héctor Rodríguez and rookie Carlos Jorge also went deep, and the Cincinnati Reds rallied from an early deficit to beat the NL East champion Atlanta Braves 7-6 on Thursday night.


With the loss, Atlanta secured the No. 3 seed for the National League playoffs, behind Milwaukee and the Los Angeles Dodgers. The Braves (93-66) will host a best-of-three Wild Card Series starting Tuesday.


Rodríguez's two-run homer in the sixth inning off AJ Smith-Shawver (0-3) made it 7-6. De La Cruz extended his career high with a shot to right field in the third, and he needs one stolen base for the fourth 30/30 season in Reds history.


Jorge led off the game with his first career homer.


Connor Phillips (2-0), the third of six Cincinnati pitchers, got four outs. Emilio Pagán worked the ninth for his 25th save.


Atlanta scored four runs in the bottom of the first, but Cincinnati quickly rallied against Tyler Mahle. The right-hander gave up five runs in five innings in his final start before the playoffs. It was his worst outing since joining the Braves from San Francisco at the trade deadline. He gave up two runs or fewer in each of his previous eight starts with Atlanta.


Braves star Ronald Acuña Jr. returned after missing one game with a bone bruise on his shin, racing around at full speed to score from first on a double in the first inning. He was 2 for 5 with a stolen base.


Reds starter Brady Singer lasted three innings and gave up five runs on seven hits. Austin Riley homered against him in the third.


Up next
Reds: Conclude the season with a three-game series at Toronto. LHP Nick Lodolo (3-6, 5.04 ERA) will oppose Blue Jays RHP José Soriano (12-8, 3.72) on Friday.


Braves: Have not announced a starter for Friday's series opener at Miami. RHP Eury Pérez (7-11, 4.14) starts for the Marlins.

stories.headline: Pelinka: Lakers grateful for run with LeBron, exit 'done amicably'
stories.summary: Rob Pelinka said Thursday that the Lakers remain thankful for their time with LeBron James.
stories.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Lakers president of basketball operations and general manager Rob Pelinka said LeBron James' decision to leave the franchise this summer was "done amicably" and that the Lakers remain thankful for their time with the all-time great.

"I thought it would be appropriate at the front to express gratitude for the LeBron era here," Pelinka said Thursday before a season-opening news conference alongside Lakers coach JJ Redick.

"Clearly, new team and new players, and that's what we're going to talk about today. But we as an organization are still grateful for the run that we had with him here."

Thursday's news conference was two months to the day since James agreed to a two-year, $8 million deal with the Philadelphia 76ers and an occasion for Pelinka to share his first remarks about James' departure.

"The Lakers have become -- as they should -- a perennial playoff team," Pelinka continued, looking back at James' eight years in L.A. "Won a championship, went to the Western Conference finals. It was a great era, and we're grateful for it. I think it's important to say that at the onset as we turn into a new chapter."

James' longtime friend and agent, Rich Paul of Klutch Sports, informed the Lakers about eight hours before the official start of free agency on June 30 that his client would be seeking a new team.

The decision was an about-face from James' previous public stance during NBA All-Star weekend in Indianapolis in February 2024.

"I am a Laker and I'm happy and been very happy being a Laker the last six years and hopefully it stays that way," James said at the time.

James' choice also came after Pelinka publicly lobbied to bring James back during an exit interview news conference with reporters in May following the Lakers' second-round exit against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

"LeBron, we probably haven't seen a player that has honored the game to the extent that he's honored the game," Pelinka said May 12. "He's given so much to his teammates, to this organization. And the thing we want to do more than anything else is honor him back. ... Any team, including ours, would love to have LeBron James on their roster."

Pelinka was asked, considering those statements from James and the Lakers in the past, why he thinks the 41-year-old star is now in Philadelphia.

"Again, we're grateful for the LeBron era," Pelinka said. "I think the communications with him this offseason were held diplomatically, professionally and honestly. I'm so thankful for the partnership that we had that continued up until this summer when a decision was made for him to play for another team. It was done amicably, professionally, gracefully. We looked at the whole thing with gratitude, because it's been an incredible era for us here."

Redick, James' former "Mind the Game" podcast co-host before stepping onto the Lakers' sidelines, did not specifically address the four-time champion's departure. Redick already showed public support for James, however, shortly after James informed L.A. he would be leaving by showing up to James' live taping of "Mind the Game" with Tyrese Haliburton at Fanatics Fest in New York in July.

Redick did endorse L.A.'s roster construction once James left, though.

"I think with this group, probably the first time in my three years here that I feel like the pieces actually fit together," Redick said.

Other than a series of tweets thanking the Lakers after announcing the Sixers as his fourth -- and final -- team he will play for before retirement, James has yet to elaborate on his L.A. exit.

Fans will not have to wait much longer to hear James' side of things. A new episode of "Mind the Game" is scheduled to be released Friday. In an Instagram post teasing the release, James' co-host, Steve Nash, asks him, "How did you come to Philly? What led to saying, like, 'That's my destination'?"

James also will address reporters for the first time since his decision when the Sixers hold their annual media day Monday in Camden, New Jersey.

stories.headline: Former England forward Andy Carroll says he was sexually assaulted by a man in 2021
stories.summary: Former England forward Andy Carroll has revealed in his autobiography he was sexually assaulted by a man during 2021.
stories.body:
Former England forward Andy Carroll has said in his autobiography he was sexually assaulted by a man during 2021.

The 37-year-old included the details in his book, titled "Owning It." As a victim of sexual assault, Carroll was automatically granted anonymity.

Carroll said the incident took place at his home during a second spell at Newcastle. The offender -- a friend of his former partner, who was staying away at the time -- was later jailed for three years, with Carroll having testified in court.

Former Liverpool and West Ham striker Carroll, who is now a player/co-owner of National League South club Dagenham & Redbridge, said the incident happened when he was sleeping. He said he then threw the man out of the house, and knocked him unconscious when he attempted to get back inside.

"I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now," wrote Carroll, who had decided to include the incident in his book "at the very last minute" after discussing it with his girlfriend, Lou Teasdale.

"Me and Lou spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not. I avoided my publisher for so long that they probably suspected I got cold feet.

"Scary to talk about but it's made [me] the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff. And if me talking about it helps just one person then good, it will have been worth it."

Carroll said testifying in court, where the attacker was found guilty of sexual offences and placed on the sex offender register, was "humiliating and embarrassing and absolutely horrendous."

The 37-year-old said: "What happened to me affected every facet of my life. I'd think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including football ... The trauma of what happened to me hasn't gone away."

stories.headline: Lachie Neale ban overturned, free to play AFL Grand Final
stories.summary: Star Brisbane midfielder Lachie Neale has been cleared to play in the AFL grand final after overturning his one-game suspension at the appeals board.
stories.body:
Star Brisbane midfielder Lachie Neale has been cleared to play in the AFL Grand Final after overturning his one-game suspension at the appeals board.

The dual Brownlow Medal winner will feature in the premiership decider against Fremantle - his former club - at the MCG on Saturday after having a striking charge on Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan downgraded on Thursday.

Neale will instead be fined $10,000.

He initially failed in challenging the one-game ban from the match review officer at the tribunal on Tuesday night.

To succeed on appeal, Brisbane had to prove the tribunal finding was either an error of law, an unreasonable decision, a manifestly excessive classification, or a manifestly excessive sanction.

The Lons were able to sway the appeals board that the tribunal had made an error of law in not considering the exceptional and compelling circumstances of Neale not having previously been suspended in 320 AFL games.

Neale avoids becoming the first player to miss an AFL grand final following a preliminary-final suspension since Collingwood's Anthony Rocca in 2003.

Brisbane legal representative Adrian Anderson tried various different arguments to clear Neale.

One included suggesting the ban should be served in round one next year, instead of in the grand final, due to the added importance of the match.

It was a bold strategy given Neale is almost certain to leave Brisbane and join Collingwood during the off-season.

Anderson leaned heavily on Neale's prior record of not being suspended, referring to the four-time All-Australian as "pretty close to a unicorn".

Introduced this year, the "exceptional and compelling circumstances" clause had been deployed once: to downgrade a one-game ban to Collingwood legend and AFL games record-holder Scott Pendlebury, to a fine.

New vision of Neale's strike on Ginnivan became available on Thursday, but was not allowed to be used because it was not shown at Tuesday's tribunal hearing.

The footage would have shown a clearer picture of the incident and likely not helped Neale's case.

Sydney's Barry Hall (2005) and Richmond's Trent Cotchin (2017) famously escaped bans for incidents in their respective preliminary finals to play in eventual premiership wins.

The Lions named Neale in their team on Thursday, shortly before the decision was handed down, and didn't need to change the 23.

With rain expected for Saturday's grand final, Neale will figure prominently as one of the Lions' best wet-weather players.

stories.headline: Arman Tsarukyan elevates his position in MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Arman Tsarukyan put on a performance at UFC 331 that makes him all but undeniable as the next challenger for the lightweight championship.

Tsarukyan has been in this position before. In January 2025, he pulled out of a title fight because of injury one day before he was to fight for the belt. Later in the year, he was twice passed over when the UFC was booking title bouts. But Saturday's elbow to the face of Mauricio Ruffy gave Tsarukyan the impressive first-round knockout he needed to position himself as the likely first challenger of champion Justin Gaethje.

Tsarukyan's victory also boosted him above former champion Ilia Topuria to No. 2 at lightweight in the latest ESPN divisional rankings.

That is the only movement in the rankings, as Saturday's main event winner, men's flyweight champion Joshua Van, already was the top-ranked 125 pounder. Ex-champ Alexandre Pantoja remains at No. 2.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

Results are current; rankings as of Sept. 22. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: V'landys sets sights on overseas moves in new NRL role
stories.summary: Peter V'landys has officially been appointed as the NRL's new executive chairman, making him the most powerful player in the sport in 30 years.
stories.body:
Peter V'landys has promised to take rugby league to the world after being handed the most powerful role in the sport since the end of the Super League war.

Hours after resigning as Racing NSW chief executive on Thursday, V'landys was officially appointed as the NRL's first executive chairman.

The veteran administrator did not front a media conference, but in a statement made clear his desire for the next era of the NRL and the possibility of a global round.

"I am honoured every day to have the opportunity to give something back to rugby league and could not be more excited for the game's future," V'landys said.

"Rugby League is the greatest game of all and we are going to take it to the world."

Since taking over as ARL Commission chairman in 2019, V'landys has become the increasingly dominant figure in rugby league.

But this move will see his role grow even further, effectively replacing former NRL chief executive Andrew Abdo while remaining at the head of the commission.

When Abdo announced his resignation as NRL chief in May, V'landys said only "Superman and Jesus added together" could possibly replace him.

At the time, V'landys refused to enter into speculation if that figure could indeed be him, but signalled he would take leave from Racing NSW in July to be able to dedicate time to the NRL.

The 64-year-old has since garnered the support required from the clubs and the states to allow him to take on the role.

Fellow commissioners have also approved the move, which comes months after V'landys and Abdo locked in a $5.3 billion media rights agreement over seven years.

In a statement, the NRL said V'landys had "overseen the most successful and transformative period in the game's history" since becoming chair.

"Peter inherited a game with limited reserves and no significant assets, one that had needed an advance from its broadcasters just to pay the clubs and players," V'landys' predecessor and fellow commissioner Peter Beattie said.

"He consistently put the fan first, and the record audiences and the biggest broadcast deal in Australian sport followed."

Since the creation of the independent ARL Commission in 2012, no person has held the role of chairman and executive on a full-time basis.

Even before the introduction of the ARLC, News Corp and the ARL had overseen the NRL following an agreement out of the Super League war.

The ARL Commission confirmed on Thursday it would also establish a governance oversight committee, chaired by Dr Gary Weiss, to ensure compliance of best-practice corporate governance.

V'landys' time as chairman was initially headlined by the NRL's handling of the COVID-19 pandemic shutdown.

Since then, expansion both at home and abroad has been the constant theme.

V'landys has signalled an intent to go to 20 teams as soon as 2029, while the entry of the PNG Chiefs shapes as the biggest change to the NRL in decades.

The Las Vegas venture has also kicked off a move towards more overseas matches, with the NRL confirming it has games planned for Hong Kong and Japan in 2028.

Meanwhile, V'landys' exit from Racing NSW brings an end to a 22-year rein at the helm of the sport, having previously also spent 17 years as boss of NSW Harness Racing.

He led the racing industry through the equine influenza outbreak, with the creation of The Everest in 2017 among other key legacy pieces.

"Naturally, this is a very sad day for me. I have put my heart and soul into racing for 22 years," V'landys said.
